ukmt-grey-2015-03.title: Find the small rectangle
ukmt-grey-2015-03.body:
Two flat rectangles are stacked and together are as tall as one upright rectangle, so the long side of a small rectangle is twice the short side: $2\times10=20$ cm. The large rectangle is made of an upright rectangle on each side and the flat ones in the middle, so its longer side is $10+20+10=40$ cm.

**Answer: (B) 40 cm**

ukmt-grey-2015-15.title: Force the colours
ukmt-grey-2015-15.body:
Every triangle needs one side of each colour. In each end triangle two sides are given (blue and green), so the third side is red. Working along the strip, each next triangle already has one forced side and one given side, which forces its third side. The side $x$ lies in a triangle that already has a blue and a red side, so $x$ must be green.

**Answer: (A) only green**

ukmt-grey-2015-16.title: Only one student can be right
ukmt-grey-2015-16.body:
All five answers are different, so at most one student is telling the truth. If nobody were telling the truth, Daniel (who said 'none') would be right, a contradiction. So exactly one student is truthful, and she is the one who said 'only one': Ellen. Exactly one student did her homework.

**Answer: (B) 1**

ukmt-grey-2015-17.title: Add the equations
ukmt-grey-2015-17.body:
The four regions that neighbour the $-4$ region have numbers $a,b,c,d$, and their sum is $-4$ (the number in the $-4$ region). The region marked $2$ has exactly the same four neighbours plus the central region, so $a+b+c+d+\,?=2$. Hence $-4+\,?=2$, so $?=6$.

**Answer: (E) 6**

ukmt-grey-2015-23.title: Use the largest distances
ukmt-grey-2015-23.body:
The five points $P,Q,R,S,T$ in order with $PT=22$ the largest distance. The next largest, 20, is $PS$ or $QT$; take $QT=20$, so $PQ=2$. The next largest is 17: it cannot involve $PR$ or $RT$ combinations giving 3, so $PS=17$ and $ST=5$. Then $QS=15$. The remaining distances $6,8,9,k$ are $PR,QR,RS,RT$ with $QR+RS=15$, so $\{QR,RS\}=\{6,9\}$. Then $PR=2+6=8$ (taking $QR=6$) and $RT=22-8=14$. So $k=14$.

**Answer: (A) 14**

ukmt-grey-2015-24.title: Aim for the form 2d+(d-1)
ukmt-grey-2015-24.body:
The remainder on dividing by $d$ is at most $d-1$. For $d\le 671$ this is at most 670. For larger $d$ up to 1000 the quotient is at least 2; with quotient 2 we get remainder $2015-2d$, which is largest for the smallest such $d$. Quotient 2 works when $2d+(d-1)\ge2015$, i.e. $d\ge 672$, and $d=672$ gives remainder $2015-1344=671$. For $d>672$ the remainder $2015-2d<671$.

**Answer: (C) 671**
